questions: If the bottom row becomes completely filled after some blocks have moved downward during a time step, does the removal of the bottom row happen immediately before those blocks move further in the same step or only at the start of the next time step?
When the bottom row is removed, are the remaining blocks' column positions preserved (i.e., do they keep the same x‑coordinate) or are they shifted in any way?
If multiple blocks would occupy the same cell after moving downward in the same time step, is that situation possible, and if so, how should it be resolved?

Does the “entire bottom row is filled” condition consider only blocks that existed at the beginning of the current time step, or does it also include blocks that have just moved into the bottom row during that step?
After the bottom row is removed, do the y‑coordinates of the remaining blocks decrease by one (i.e., does the whole grid collapse upward) or do they stay at the same absolute row numbers?
Are the time steps indexed starting from t = 1 after the initial configuration at t = 0, and does the removal rule apply at t = 1 before any movement occurs?

Can the value of W be larger than the number of distinct X‑coordinates among the blocks, and if so, does it affect the “entire bottom row is filled” condition (i.e., must every column from 1 to W contain a block)?
If a query asks about a block that has already been removed in a previous time step, should the answer be “No” for all later times, and is there any possibility of a removed block reappearing later?

inline_prompts: There is a grid with 10^9 rows and W columns. The cell at the x-th column from the left and the y-th row from the bottom is denoted by (x,y). There are N blocks. Each block is a 1 \times 1 square, and block i-th (1 \leq i \leq N) is located at cell (X_i,Y_i) at time 0. At times t=1,2,\dots,10^{100}, the blocks are moved according to the following rules: - If the entire bottom row is filled with blocks, then all blocks in the bottom row are removed. - For each remaining block, perform the following: - If the block is in the bottom row, or if there is a block in the cell immediately below it, do nothing. - Otherwise, move the block one cell downward. You are given Q queries. For the j-th query (1 \leq j \leq Q), answer whether block A_j exists at time T_j. Input The input is given from Standard Input in the following format: N W X_1 Y_1 X_2 Y_2 \vdots X_N Y_N Q T_1 A_1 T_2 A_2 \vdots T_Q A_Q Output Print Q lines. Constraints - 1 \leq N \leq 2 \times 10^5 - 1 \leq W \leq N - 1 \leq X_i \leq W - 1 \leq Y_i \leq 10^9 - (X_i,Y_i) \neq (X_j,Y_j) if i \neq j. - 1 \leq Q \leq 2 \times 10^5 - 1 \leq T_j \leq 10^9 - 1 \leq A_j \leq N - All input values are integers.
